Robocopy is the best file-copying tool built into Windows, and one of the hardest to remember: dozens of switches, several of which can delete files at the destination. **Mirror** lets you build the command visually instead. It covers every option in `robocopy /?` (97 settings), explains what each one does, and warns before anything can delete files. It runs entirely in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

Mirror began as a single-page Robocopy GUI in 2025 and was redesigned as part of **Conduit**, a pair of command builders that share one design system. Its sister app is [Fetch](../wget-gui/index.qmd), the Wget builder.

## How it works

1. **Pick a starting point.** Choose a preset (Daily backup, Exact mirror, Archive with permissions, Fast LAN copy, or Move and clean up) or start from scratch.
2. **Fill in the tabs.** Locations, What to do, Filters, Preserve, Performance, Automation, Logging and Advanced. Rarely used options stay hidden until you turn on **Show advanced**.
3. **Watch the command.** It updates as you choose, with every flag explained.
4. **Add to queue.** Build several jobs, reorder them, then download one `.bat` or `.ps1` script. Stop on first failure is on by default.

::: {.callout-caution}
## Some options delete files
The `/MIR` (mirror), move and purge options can remove files from the destination. The app shows a clear notice for each of them before anything can be deleted, so read it before you run the script.
:::

## Other ways in

- **Find an option.** Type a name or a flag, such as `retry` or `/MT`, to search every tab at once.
- **Paste a command.** Paste an existing `robocopy` command and the form fills in. Flags the builder does not recognise are kept under Advanced.
- **Command palette.** `Ctrl+K` jumps to any option, preset or page, and `Ctrl+Enter` adds the current command to the queue.
- **Profiles.** Save a full set of options and load it later. Profiles, the queue and the form are remembered in your browser.

## Technical details

The whole app is one self-contained `index.html` with no build step to run it, so it is light and fast and works from GitHub Pages. It is generated from a shared source, so Mirror and Fetch keep identical design tokens and components. A jsdom smoke test covers it. Icons are from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) and the fonts are Bricolage Grotesque, Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono. The code lives in the [source repository](https://github.com/ar-puuk/robocopy-gui).

## Use cases

- System administrators managing file synchronization
- IT professionals setting up backup routines
- Anyone copying large directory structures with specific parameters
- Learning Robocopy syntax by seeing what each option does
